none: Verse translations only; no commentary claim beyond the translated text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king convenes a large body of leading scholars and sages to hear his troubling dream.
rows.anchor: meşhur ulemâ ve hukemâsının a‘yânından mürekkeb büyük bir heyet toplamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His request for a ruling means the dream is important to him and he wants its interpretation to resolve his difficulty.
rows.anchor: bu rüya, benim için pek mühim bir mesele oldu, bunu tâbir edip müşkilimi hallediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The court dismisses the dream as a meaningless jumble, like old and new grass mixed together, and says it cannot interpret dreams.
rows.anchor: yaşı kurusuna karışmış ot demetleri gibi yenisi eskisine karışmış bir yığın uyku hayâlâtı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic usage distinguishes ru'yā, a dream with a real meaning beyond its images, from hulm, an empty delusion or false inner or satanic event.
rows.anchor: Kur’an ihtar ediyor ki “rüya” “ahlâm”dan başkadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ordinary speech treats ru'yā and hulm as synonyms, ru'yā derives from seeing and points through its mental image to an underlying reality.
rows.anchor: “Rüya”, “rü’yet” mânasından me’huz olduğu için bunda hayâlin mâverâsında bir hakikat görülmüş bulunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation crosses from imagined forms to the reality behind them; in Arabic, ubūr or ibāra is more eloquent than the customary ta'bīr.
rows.anchor: “ubûru’r-rü’yâ”, “ibâretü’r-rü’yâ” denilmek Arabîde daha fasihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'wīl al-aḥādīth can mean grasping the real import of words or the eventual meaning and outcome of events, since ḥadīth can mean speech or an event.
rows.anchor: “Ehâdîs” “hadîs”in cem‘i, “hadîs” de söz veya hâdis, yani hâdise demek olabileceğine göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difference between true dreams and empty dreams parallels the difference between truthful and false speech or accurate and mistaken perceptions while awake.
rows.anchor: yakaza hâlinde doğru bir söz veya hakīkī bir ihtisas ile eğri bir sözün veya yanlış bir ihtisâsın farkları ne ise rüya ile ahlâm beynindeki fark da o demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams usually encode a person's hidden consciousness as a riddle or symbolic parable, and interpreting them requires bestowed insight, from intuition or inspiration up to revelation.
rows.anchor: ekseriyetle rüyalar örf-i âm ile değil, ferdin nefsindeki gizli şuur husûsiyetlerine göre söyleyen bir muamma

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A non-prophet's dream or interpretation generally yields no certain knowledge, though it can produce individual conviction at varying degrees of confidence.
rows.anchor: enbiyâdan mâ‘adâsının rüyası ve tâbiri sûret-i umûmiyede ilm-i yakīn ifade etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actual events can verify a dream's interpretation: some dreams occur exactly, some are interpreted as they are seen, and some bring an inarticulate but compelling sense of truth.
rows.anchor: Rüyanın asıl tevili vâkı‘ât ile tebeyyün eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king's dream belongs to the kind that its dreamer senses to be true but cannot interpret, which is why he asks the court for an explanation.
rows.anchor: Mevzû‘-i bahis olan Mısır melikinin rüyası da böyle olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the court, the king seems to recognize his vision as a meaningful dream rather than an empty jumble, even though he cannot interpret it himself.
rows.anchor: Mevzû‘-i bahis olan Mısır melikinin rüyası da böyle olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic scholars classify dreams as divine instruction, self-generated recollections with no independent value, or satanic false associations; the latter two are ahlām.
rows.anchor: Ulemâ-yı İslâm, rüya hâdiselerini üç sınıf üzerine tasnif etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report that a dream is one forty-sixth of prophecy points to its epistemic value, while the report that glad tidings remain after prophecy ends highlights its emotional value.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfi ilmî haysiyetine işaret olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's mission lasted twenty-three years, with revelation in its first six months arriving through dreams like true dawn; six months is one forty-sixth of that span.
rows.anchor: bu yirmi üç sene müddetin ilk altı ayındaki vahiy de hep fecr-i sâdık gibi zuhur eden rüya ile olmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams and even confused dreams can matter for self-knowledge because they stir feelings, not only because they may convey knowledge.
rows.anchor: ahlâmın bile ma‘rifetü’n-nefste şâyân-ı mütalaa bir ehemmiyeti vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waking perception combines a present sensation with memories of similar past sensations; association among them lets a person recognize and describe what is seen or heard.
rows.anchor: birtakım suver ü me‘ânî dahi tedâ‘î ve tevârüd etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep also exposes the self to external or internal impressions and lets past memories associate, producing dream experiences without voluntary attention or control.
rows.anchor: hâtırât-ı mâziyesi tedâ‘î edebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associations made only from past memories form empty dreams, whereas associations prompted by an influence from God form true dreams.
rows.anchor: Taraf-ı Hak’tan bir tesir üzerine cereyan eden tedâ‘îler de rüyayı teşkil ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike waking perception, dreams unfold involuntarily beyond choice; this makes direct divine instruction more evident in dreams, even though their meaning is less clear.
rows.anchor: rüya hâdisesi ise nefsin irade ve intihâbı fevkinde ve mücerred cebrî bir surette cereyan eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bright waking visions, especially in darkness or with closed eyes, can later prove true like dreams; both reveal reality to the spirit through an imaginal realm between meaning and matter.
rows.anchor: âlem-i me‘ânî ile mücerred âlem-i madde arasında mu‘allak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation cannot be solved by logic alone; people ignorant of the unseen and God's knowledge and wisdom may consequently claim all dreams are empty fantasies.
rows.anchor: esrâr-ı gaybiyeden büsbütün gāfil olanlar, Rabbü’l-âlemîn’in alîm ve hakîm olduğunu bilmeyenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survivor is the cupbearer who had asked Yusuf to interpret the dreams; after a long interval he remembered Yusuf and offered to explain the king's dream.
rows.anchor: uzun bir müddet sonra -bu vesile ile- hatırlayıp dedi

none: Verse translations only; the remaining phrase merely introduces the next passage.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing the cupbearer's account, the king recognizes Yusuf's learning and virtue and orders that he be brought from prison.
rows.anchor: Melik, Yûsuf’un ilm ü fazlını anladı ve zindandan çıkarılıp kendisine getirilmesini emreyledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf refuses to leave immediately and asks for a public inquiry into the women who cut their hands, so his innocence and unjust imprisonment become clear to others; God already knows the truth.
rows.anchor: benim sırf kadın hîlesiyle bi-gayri hakkın hapsedildiğim enzâr-ı âmmede anlaşılsın, ismet ü berâetim gereği gibi tebeyyün eylesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf avoids naming the chief's wife and has remained unshaken through years in prison, showing exceptional restraint and dignity.
rows.anchor: Ve şâyân-ı dikkattir ki asıl hanımı tasrih etmedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king appreciates Yusuf's concern and personally summons and interrogates the women to investigate the matter.
rows.anchor: Bunu takdir eden Melik de bizzat tahkīkāta girişip kadınları ihzar ve istintak ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the next two verses seem by their content to be Yusuf's words, their connection to the preceding passage makes the chief's wife's speech continuing more apparent.
rows.anchor: mâkabline irtibâtı cihetiyle hanımın kelâmının mâba‘di olması daha zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's question makes the brothers' earlier revelation come true: they would be told of their deed while unaware of his identity.
rows.anchor: لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ [Yûsuf 12/15] vahiy ve vaadinin mısdâkı tamamen tahakkuk etmiş oluyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's words strike the brothers suddenly, and they infer in astonishment that the speaker is Yusuf before asking him directly.
rows.anchor: derhâl onun Yûsuf olduğuna intikal ederek kemâl-i hayret ve heyecan ile kekelercesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf identifies himself and his brother, who is beside him in a position of honor and had seemed to escape their notice.
rows.anchor: mevki‘-i ikbalde bulunan ve nazar-ı dikkatinizden kaçmış gibi görünen zât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid sounding proud, Yusuf gives thanks to God and teaches that God does not waste the reward of those who fear Him and remain patient.
rows.anchor: gurur ve tefâhur hissi anlaşılmamak için Allah’a şükür ve tahdîs-i ni‘met ile nasihat makamında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The household Yusuf asks for includes the entire family of Yaqub, men and women, young and old.
rows.anchor: bütün ehlinizi -yani erkek dişi, büyük küçük hânedân-ı Ya‘kūb’a mensup bütün ailenizi-

rows.speaker: رواية
rows.claim: A report says Judah takes the shirt, saying he had first brought grief with the bloodied shirt and will now bring good news.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki gömleği kardeşleri içinden Yehûda

rows.speaker: رواية
rows.claim: The same report says Judah runs barefoot from Egypt to Canaan, a distance of eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: yalın ayak başı kabak Mısır’dan Ken‘an’a koşmuş ve aradaki mesafe seksen fersah imiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf would certainly equip this family caravan even better than he equipped his brothers on earlier journeys.
rows.anchor: evvelki defalarda kardeşlerini techiz eden Yûsuf’un bu kere bu emirleri verirken iktizâ eden levâzımı ile elbette daha mükemmel surette techiz edip uğrattığını

rows.speaker: رواية
rows.claim: A report says Yusuf sent two hundred riding camels with provisions for his father.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre bu kafilede babasına iki yüz râhile techiz etmiş göndermişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author anticipates the spiritual joy and reunion that will unfold when the family's good fortune arrives.
rows.anchor: nasıl bir neş’e ve revhâniyet kaynaşacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqub asks his listeners to trust his senses and not call him senile, since they had already rejected even his earlier grief over Yusuf.
rows.anchor: de vicdânıma itimad etseydiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The approaching caravan's news and Yusuf's fragrance bring Yaqub a spiritual foretaste of reunion and gradually prepare him for the joy to come.
rows.anchor: bu Yûsuf kokusu şüphe yok ki ona

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fragrance reaches Yaqub from far away too quickly for ordinary wind, and his heightened sensitivity alone cannot explain why he sensed it only when the caravan departed.
rows.anchor: Seksen fersahlık bir mesafeden bu rayihayı getiren nâkil ne idi? Ve bunu duyan hassasiyet nasıl bir hassasiyetti?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators offer two explanations: God miraculously conveyed the scent into Yaqub's conscience or directly created it there.
rows.anchor: müfessirînin bu hususta iki ifadesi vardır. Birisi Allah teâlâ’nın bu râyihayı bir mucize olmak üzere o uzak mesafeden Ya‘kūb’un vicdânına îsâl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Current science can transmit sound electrically but, as the author observes, it does not yet know how to use electricity to transmit scent or smell.
rows.anchor: henüz râyiha işine ve şem hissine hizmetini bilmiyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqub's hearers resist believing him and treat his earlier longing as irrational, so he asks not to be dismissed as senile.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf kokusuna ve henüz vicdânımdan başka hiçbir delîli görünmeyen bu sözüme, bu ledünnî vuslat müjdecisine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human knowledge cannot fully explain distant sensation or even ordinary perception; the verse permits such experiences without requiring a forced explanation, as knowledge remains limited.
rows.anchor: Bunlar bilinmeden uzaktan his hâdise-i rûhiyesini mutlaka tevile mecburiyet yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts feeling sudden sorrow about his uncle at the moment of his death, then learning fifteen days later by letter that the uncle had died then and left him books.
rows.anchor: On beş gün sonra memleketten posta ile mektup aldım, pederim o gün amcamın vefat ettiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls such distant impressions telepathy, groups them with inspiration, and says the same experience during sleep would be called a dream; they are common but not ordinary sources of knowledge.
rows.anchor: bizim ıstılâhımız bütün bunları ilham cümlesinden saymaktı ve bu hâl uykuda iken olsa idi aynen rüya derdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Telepathic impressions range from ordinary delusion to levels of certainty that may reach the rank of a saintly wonder or miracle.
rows.anchor: Alelâde bir vehim hâlinde keramet veya mucize mertebelerine kadar çıkacak muhtelif derecâtta zâhir olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's word rīḥ suggests conveyance; the author speculates that scent may travel through electrical waves and that scent itself may be a transferable force or vibration worth investigating scientifically.
rows.anchor: meseleyi kimya veya zerrevî fizik sahasında tâkip ederek savt naklinden daha ince bir kanun ile râyiha kuvvet ve hareketinin zabt u naklinde dahi elektrik cereyânından istifade mümkin olduğu neticesine varabilecek demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if a hidden law carries the scent, the event remains miraculous through God's control of its emission, extraordinary speed, and Yaqub's recognition; discovering a law does not erase the miracle.
rows.anchor: Gerek bu cihetlerden ve gerekse Ya‘kūb ve Yûsuf’un birer peygamber olmaları haysiyetiyle vak‘a i‘câzkârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers call Yaqub's hope an old delusion, but the approaching reunion will soon reveal whose judgment was mistaken.
rows.anchor: çok geçmeden şaşkınlık kimde olduğu tebeyyün etti

none: Verse translations only; no explanatory commentary in this segment.
Verse translation only; no explanatory commentary in this segment.
Verse translation and transition only; no distinct commentary claim in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the first verse revealed about intoxicants; although it does not yet prohibit wine, contrasting intoxicant with good provision shows it is not good.
rows.anchor: bu âyet müskirâta dair ilk nâzil olan âyettir. Bununla şarap henüz tahrim edilmiş olmamakla beraber görülüyor ki “rızk-ı hasen”e mukabil zikredilmiş ve binâen‘aleyh güzel bir şey olmadığı anlatılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between intoxicant and good provision parallels the preceding contrast between milk and filth and blood, hinting that intoxicants are impure.
rows.anchor: “rızk-ı hasen” ile “seker”in tekabülü süt ile fers ve demin tekabülüne nazîrdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good provision here means molasses and other sweet products.
rows.anchor: “rızk-ı hasen” pekmez ve ma‘mûlâtı gibi tatlılardır

none: Verse translations only; no explanatory commentary in this segment.
